common.ops_best_practices: Best practices: anticipate peaks (seasonality, public holidays), use proper export packaging (blocking, strapping), secure ad valorem insurance and keep a buffer on critical deadlines.
common.incoterms_intro: Incoterms shift control, cost allocation and risk transfer along the chain. Typical patterns: FOB/CIF for standard sea flows; DAP/DDP for door-to-door experience.
incoterms_list: FOB: buyer controls main carriage; requires logistics maturity
CFR: seller pays main carriage; risk transfers at loading
CIF: seller pays freight + insurance; risk transfers at loading
DAP/DDP: extended coverage by seller; import clearance and taxes depending on variant
common.delivered_cost_note: Always compare FCL vs LCL on total delivered cost, not only on the rate per m³.

common.cbm_note: Indicative only: 20' ≈ 33 m³, 40' ≈ 67 m³. Tolerances and weight/volume limits depend on carrier and service.

france_angola.label: France ↔ Angola
france_angola.title: Sea freight France ↔ Angola (FCL & LCL)
france_angola.subtitle: Specialised in LCL groupage, FCL full containers, international moves and vehicle/motorbike shipping to Luanda from France and Europe (France/Benelux), for both businesses and individuals, including parcels, baggage and personal effects in containers or groupage. As a France‑based freight forwarder working with multiple ocean carriers, we prioritise service quality, reliable lead times and coherent pricing rather than purely “cheapest at any cost” rates.
france_angola.transit: Indicative transit times: 20–25 days depending on port of departure, rotations and season.
costs: To Luanda, LCL (groupage) is particularly relevant for small volumes, personal effects and B2B parcels. Above roughly 13–15 m³, FCL usually becomes more competitive and offers more predictable lead times.

Costs should be assessed as total delivered cost: sea freight, surcharges, port THC, pre/post-carriage and duties/taxes on import into Angola. We help you arbitrate between LCL/FCL and French/Benelux departure ports according to your budget and deadlines.

Whether you are shipping garments, e‑commerce parcels, industrial pallets or a full move with vehicles, we build a transparent cost breakdown and clearly explain what is included (freight, surcharges, handling, pre/post‑carriage, estimated duties and taxes).
customs: Angola requires strict documentation: detailed commercial invoice, packing list, BL, certificate of origin where applicable and cargo-specific documents. We assist with HS classification, duty/tax estimates and file preparation to reduce inspections and delays.
insurance_risks: Ad valorem cargo insurance sized to the value of your goods
Export packaging advice (wooden crates, reinforced pallets, wrapping and blocking) to reduce damage
Visibility on key milestones (loading, transhipment, arrival) and proactive follow-up with local stakeholders

services_block.title: End-to-end logistics services for your shipments to Angola (Luanda)
services_block.intro: For your Angola flows, we do more than just book a container: we coordinate the whole logistics chain from France and Europe to Luanda port, including:
items: Pick-up and delivery of partial loads (pallets, cartons, personal effects, small B2B shipments) across France and the Benelux.
Pre- and post-carriage for FCL containers to the departure port and from Luanda port, organising road transport where feasible via our partner network.
Transport documentation management (ocean bill of lading, packing list, commercial invoice and specific certificates required by the cargo type).
Export customs clearance in France and support with import formalities in Angola through our local partners.
LCL sea freight services to Luanda for intermediate volumes, with consolidation and warehousing options in France or the Benelux before departure.
Handling of export, import and, on a case-by-case basis, cross-trade operations involving Angola.
Assistance with the preparation of shipping certificates required by Angolan authorities, in coordination with partners located near the country’s main ports.

why_us: Dedicated positioning on the France–Angola corridor for all types of shipments (B2B cargo, international moves, vehicles and motorbikes).
Experience on the France/Europe ↔ Luanda corridor, covering LCL groupage, FCL and vehicles.
Partner network in Antwerp/Rotterdam to optimise capacity, costs and transit times.
Route-specific documentation support for Angola and coordination with local counterparts.
use_cases: International moves and personal effects (boxes, furniture, household goods) in LCL or FCL to Luanda, with pickup options in France and the Benelux.
Textile and ready-to-wear shipments (cartons, bales, accessories) for retail and e‑commerce flows into Angola.
B2B shipments (pallets, spare parts, consumables, equipment) in LCL or FCL depending on volume and flow regularity.
Machinery and equipment: FCL, Open Top or special equipment after feasibility study, with organised road pre-carriage.
Vehicles and motorbikes: tailored Ro-Ro or container solutions with on-wheels loading without dismantling whenever possible, documentation management and coordinated delivery on site.

planning: Anticipate peak periods (year end, project roll-outs) and secure sailings with sufficient notice.
Compare departures from France (Le Havre / Fos) and from Antwerp/Rotterdam to optimise lead times and budget.
Switch to FCL as soon as value and volume justify it, to reduce handling and stabilise transit times.
documentation: Ensure detailed invoices (clear description, realistic value, origin) to avoid revaluation and blocks.
Validate any local specific requirements (licences, permits, technical documents) before shipping.
Document packaging (dated photos, package IDs) and keep evidence needed for insurance and claims.
kpis: Average time between vessel arrival and customs release in Luanda.
Gap between actual cost and quote (including duties/taxes).

faq.a: Yes. Groupage is relevant for personal effects, small lots and professional parcels. We operate regular departures to Luanda with visibility on key milestones.

faq.q: When should we switch from LCL to FCL to Luanda?
faq.a: In practice, FCL often becomes attractive above roughly 13–15 m³, considering total delivered cost and the sensitivity of the goods.

faq.q: Which documents are required for Angola?
faq.a: Detailed commercial invoice, packing list, BL, certificates of origin or specific documents depending on the goods, and paperwork required by Angolan authorities. We guide you through this checklist.

faq.q: Can you handle vehicles or personal effects?
faq.a: Yes, subject to feasibility review: vehicles in containers or Ro-Ro, motorbikes on their wheels without dismantling whenever possible, personal effects in LCL or FCL. We clarify customs and regulatory constraints upfront.

faq.q: Do you recommend insurance for Angola?
faq.a: Yes, an ad valorem policy is strongly recommended on this corridor. We help size coverage and document packaging to reduce disputes.

faq.q: How much does it cost to ship a 20' or 40' container to Luanda?
faq.a: The cost of a 20' or 40' container to Luanda depends on the departure port (Le Havre, Fos, Antwerp, Rotterdam), season, cargo type and the services included (pre/post-carriage, customs, cargo insurance). We provide detailed, itemised quotes (ocean freight, surcharges, THC, estimated duties & taxes) so you have a clear view of total delivered cost.

faq.q: Which lead time should we plan for a full move from France to Angola?
faq.a: On average, you should allow 20–25 days of sea transit to Luanda, plus time for pickup, stuffing, port operations and customs clearance on arrival. We recommend planning a buffer for potential inspections and scheduling your move as soon as your approximate dates are known.
